section.title: How to Locate the Log File and the Log Configuration File
section.p: To locate the Log file where the logs are written, or the Config file used to configure logging, go to the Administration Page, and in the General tab, you can view the location of these files. uses Logback as its logging implementation. For backward compatibility and simplicity, log levels can also be specified using the Log4j 1 syntax, but Log4j itself is not used for logging.

section.title: Logging Configuration Files
section.p: Logging is controlled by the following two configuration files, both located in the WEB-INF directory of the deployed web application:

row.entry: It uses the standard Logback syntax and controls all aspects of logging (appenders, the location and rotation of the log file, the layout of the messages, and the log levels).

An optional file that is kept for backward compatibility. Only log levels specified in the Log4j 1 syntax (log4j.category.logger.name=level) are read from this file. Any other type of configuration must be added in logback.xml.

section.p:
If the same logger is configured in more than one place, the following precedence applies, from the highest to the lowest:
logging.level.* system properties
WEB-INF/log4j.properties
WEB-INF/logback.xml
section.note: The logback.configurationFile system property is not taken into account because the configuration files are loaded explicitly from the WEB-INF directory.

section.title: Enabling HTTP Request Logging for Debugging
section.p: To enable a detailed logging of the HTTP requests sent by , edit the file listed as the Config file in the Administration Page, and add the following lines:log4j.category.org.apache.http.impl.conn=debug log4j.category.org.apache.http.impl.client=debug log4j.category.org.apache.http.client=debug log4j.category.org.apache.http.headers=debug

Making changes to this file requires that you restart the applicationrestart the application.After you finish your debugging session, remember to revert this configuration file back to its original content to avoid performance issues.

section.title: How to Configure Logging Using a System Property
section.p: You can enable logging by setting system properties. For example, to enable debug logging for the category org.apache.http.client, set this system property:-Dlogging.level.org.apache.http.client=debug
